tagline: Leading North American diversified financial services provider
hero_kpi_rationale: Loan book is the primary driver of net interest income, the central engine of TD's commercial and retail banking. Its growth directly reflects balance sheet expansion and market share gains in North America.
company_description: The Toronto-Dominion Bank, together with its subsidiaries, provides various financial products and services in Canada, the United States, and internationally. It operates through four segments: Canadian Personal and Commercial Banking; U.S. Retail; Wealth Management and Insurance; and Wholesale Banking. The company offers personal deposits, such as chequing, savings, and investment products; financing, investment, cash management, international trade, and banking services to businesses; and financing options to customers at point of sale for automotive and recreational vehicle purchases. It also provides credit cards and payments; real estate secured lending, auto finance, and consumer lending services; point-of-sale payment solutions for large and small businesses; wealth and asset management products, and advice to retail and institutional clients through direct investing, advice-based, and asset management businesses; and property and casualty insurance, as well as life and health insurance products. The company also provides capital markets, and corporate and investment banking products and services, including underwriting and distribution of new debt and equity issues; advice on strategic acquisitions and divestitures; and trading, funding, and investment services to corporations, governments, and institutions. The Toronto-Dominion Bank was founded in 1855 and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

kpis.name: Loan Book
kpis.explanation: Total amount of loans extended to customers, the basis of interest income.
kpis.description: Loan book reached $695.8 billion in 2025, up 6.2% year-over-year, supported by residential and commercial demand.
kpis.signal: Solid loan portfolio growth in 2025, driven by the Canadian segment and US retail banking.

kpis.name: Net Interest Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between interest income and interest expense, expressed as a percentage of earning assets.
kpis.description: NIM stood at 2.15% in 2025, up 12 basis points year-over-year, benefiting from rising rates and optimized balance sheet management.
kpis.signal: Margin improvement thanks to favorable interest rate positioning.

kpis.name: Return on Equity
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by shareholders' equity, measures performance for the shareholder.
kpis.description: Return on equity reached 14.8% in 2025, up 80 basis points, driven by margin improvement and cost discipline.
kpis.signal: ROE progressing toward the strategic target of 15-17%.

kpis.name: Common Equity Tier 1 Ratio (CET1)
kpis.explanation: Regulatory measure of financial strength, essential for dividends and buybacks.
kpis.description: CET1 ratio reached 12.7% in 2025, up 30 basis points, exceeding regulatory requirements and supporting capital return policies.
kpis.signal: High CET1 ratio, offering flexibility for capital return.

kpis.name: Cost-to-Income Ratio
kpis.explanation: Share of costs in total revenue: lower = more efficient.
kpis.description: The cost-to-income ratio fell to 56.4% in 2025, thanks to process optimization and revenue growth.

kpis.name: Wealth Management Assets Under Management
kpis.explanation: Total assets managed for affluent clients, a source of recurring revenue.
kpis.description: Wealth management AUM reached $489.2 billion in 2025, up 7.5% year-over-year.
kpis.signal: Robust growth driven by equity markets and client acquisition.

kpis.name: Canadian P&C Net Income
kpis.explanation: Measures the bank's net profit in Canada for personal and small business banking services.

kpis.name: U.S. Retail Net Income
kpis.explanation: Measures the profit generated by TD's US retail banking, showing the profitability of this key activity.

kpis.name: Wealth & Insurance Net Income
kpis.explanation: Measures the net income of TD Bank's wealth management and insurance division.

kpis.name: Wholesale Net Income
kpis.explanation: Measures the profit TD Bank earns from its corporate and professional investor clients.

kpis.name: AML Remediation Spend
kpis.explanation: Measures spending to remediate anti-money-laundering non-compliance, showing regulatory commitment.

kpis.name: Liquidity Coverage Ratio
kpis.explanation: Measures whether the bank has enough liquidity to survive 30 days of crisis without borrowing.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.78 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $7.663 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 37.3% in the latest year.

risks.description: Record US$3 billion sanction for anti-money-laundering (AML) failures in 2024, with an asset cap imposed by US regulators limiting US growth.
risks.score_rationale: Score 5/5. Position: dominant 2024-2025 risk. Intensity: historic fine + asset cap constraining strategy. Trend: materialized. Regulatory category, very heavy weighting.

risks.description: Exposure to the Canadian real estate market and recession risk in Canada impacting loan portfolio quality.
risks.score_rationale: Score 4/5. Position: credit quality section. Intensity: PCL ratio rising. Trend: heightened monitoring. Credit category, fundamental for a bank.

risks.description: Intense competition in the United States (TD Bank in the Northeast) with regional banks and major national banks.
risks.score_rationale: Score 3/5. Position: competition section. Intensity: margin pressure. Stable trend. Competition category.

risks.description: Growing cyber threats on banking systems with rising compliance and investment costs.
risks.score_rationale: Score 4/5. Position: IT/cyber section. Intensity: major operational risk for a bank. Trend: rising. Cyber category heavily weighted.

risks.description: NIM sensitivity to the Canadian and US rate curves, impact on net interest income.
risks.score_rationale: Score 3/5. Position: ALM section. Intensity: quantified sensitivity. Trend: cycle normalization. Rate category.

ai_positioning.summary: TD is gradually integrating artificial intelligence into its customer services and risk management, without positioning itself as a technology leader. The focus is on improving customer experience and operational efficiency.
